out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Records, Parasite Destruction, Farm-Raised
violations.observation: The following farm-raised fish served or sold in a ready-to-eat form without freezing for parasite destruction is not properly identified as such: OBSERVED SMOKED SALMON SERVED AT THE FACILITY. EHS CANNOT DETERMINE FROM THE LETTER OF PARASITE DESTRUCTION IF THE SMOKED SALMON IS PERMITTED TO BE SERVED TO A HIGHLY SUSCEPTIBLE POPULATION.
violations.corrective_action: If raw or partially cooked fish are served or sold in ready-to-eat form and the fish is raised and fed as specified by Law, a written agreement or statement from the supplier or aquaculturist stipulating that the fish were raised and fed shall be obtained by the person in charge and retained in the records for 90 calendar days beyond the time of service or sale to a consumer. PIC AGREED TO DISCONTINUE SERVING THIS SMOKED SALMON. PIC WILL ENSURE HOT SMOKED SALMON (AND A LETTER OF PARASITE DESTRUCTION) IS PROVIDED TO THE EHS PRIOR TO SERVING SMOKED SALMON AGAIN.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: In the walk-in refrigerator, raw turkey and raw fish were improperly stored. They were being stored next to one another besides being organized by their cook temperatures.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). EHS DISCUSSED CORRECT RAW ORGANIZATION WITH PIC. PIC THEN MOVED THE RAW TURKEY TO BELOW THE RAW FISH IN THE WALK-IN COOLER.

violations.title: Food Contact Surfaces Clean to Sight & Touch
violations.observation: The following equipment/utensils were observed soiled to sight and touch: the bowl for the large stand mixer for baked goods, the can opener in the kitchen, a potato slicer and muffin and cake pans were all dirty to sight and touch.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to the sight and touch. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT MULTIPLE ITEMS IN THE KITCHEN WERE DIRTY TO SIGHT AND TOUCH. PIC MOVED THE DIRTY MUFFIN AND CAKE PANS TO THE 3 VAT SINK IN ORDER TO BE WASHED, RINSED AND SANITIZED. THEN PIC DISCUSSED WITH EHS THAT THEY WILL HAVE AN EMPLOYEE BEGIN CLEANING THE LARGE MIXING BOWL FOR THE STAND MIXER, THE CAN OPENER AND THE POTATO SLICER AFTER PREP FOR DINNER SERVCE WAS COMPLETE.

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: The ice machine was dirty to sight and touch. The ice machine was dirty on the inside and is in need of a deep cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. PLEASE DEEP CLEAN THE ICE MACHINE IN THE KITCHEN BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food, Disposition
violations.observation: Observed the following ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food being held for more than the specified time/temperature allowed: Coconut cream in the walk-in refrigerator was kept after 7 days. The coconut cream was opened on 6/8/26. The coconut cream had been in the walk-in for 9 days.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL FOODS CAN ONLY BE KEPT AND USED FOR 7 DAYS, EVEN IF THE FOOD PRODUCT IS FROM A CAN. PIC DISCARDED THE COCONUT CREAM. BRIGHTVIEW DULLES CORNER (Inspection Date: 06/17/2026) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: RTE TCS Commercially Processed Food, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is commercially processed is not used or discarded within 24 hours of when the original container was opened and is not observed to be date marked: commercially processed pico salsa in both 3) Reach-in #1 and in 4) Beverage-Air 1DR UPR cooler did not have a date mark on it once it had been opened and used. Also in 1) Reach-in #2, arugula that was being stored inside, did not have a date mark on it. Inside the walk-in refrigerator, open deli mat packages also did not have a date mark on them.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety commercially processed foods when opened and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of the original container was opened. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. This date cannot exceed any manufacturer determined 'use-by' date based on food safety. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL FOODS, EVEN COMMERCIALLY PREPARED FOODS NEED TO HAVE A DATE MARK PLACED ON THEM ONCE THEY HAVE BEEN OPENED. PIC WILL EDUCATE STAFF ON HOW TO PROPERLY DATE MARK COMMERCIALLY PROCESSED ITEMS.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Storage of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. Degreaser and disinfectant surface spray was being stored on a shelf over the 3 vat sink.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored below food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items to prevent contamination. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL CHEMICALS SHOULD HAVE A SEPARATE STORAGE AREA.

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. PLEASE MAKE SURE TO LABEL ALL BOTTLES THAT CHEMICALS ARE DISTRIBUTED INTO WITH A LABEL. ANY SPRAY BOTTLES OR SQUIRT BOTTLES THAT MAY HAVE CHEMICALS IN IT, NEEDS A LABEL.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: ROP fish observed thawing in the walk-in cooler, still in ROP packing and had not cracked the seal.
violations.corrective_action: PLEASE MAKE SURE TO OPEN ROP FISH PACKAGING AS SOON AS THE THAWING PROCESS HAS BEGUN.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Controlling Pests, Pest Control Methods
violations.observation: Drain flies were found in the dish area of the kitchen during time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Insects and other pests are capable of transmitting disease to people by contaminating food and food-contact surfaces. If pests are found on the premises methods shall be used to control their presence. PIC DISCUSSED WITH EHS THAT A PEST CONTROL OPERATOR HAD ALREADY BEEN CALLED AND WILL HAVE WEEKLY TREATMENTS UNTIL THE DRAIN FLIES ARE GONE.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping clothes were being stored in chemical sanitizer solution that was greater than the required 150ppm-400ppm for quaternary ammonia sanitizer. The ppm of the sanitizer solution was 500ppm.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL WET WIPING CLOTHES MUST BE STORED IN A QUATERNARY AMMONIA SANITIZER SOLUTION OF 150PPM-400PPM. PIC DUMPED OUT SANITIZER AND WILL CALL TECHNICIAN TO FIX SANITIZER SOLUTION.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Single-service items were observed reused for the storage of multiple food items in the walk-in refrigerator and freezer. Such as a container that was storing squash was being reused to store thawing fish. As well as cooked potatoes were being stored in a container that once stored raw carrots. Also, on the walk-in freezer, granola was being stored in a container that was used to store potatoes.
violations.corrective_action: Single-service items may not be reused. PLEASE MAKE SURE TO STOP USING SINGLE SERVICE ITEMS TO STORE DIFFERENT FOODS THEN THE ONES DELIVERED IN THEM. PLEASE MAKE SURE TO STOP USING AND THROW AWAY ALL SINGLE USE CONTAINERS BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Cutting Board, When to Resurface or Discard
violations.observation: The cutting board(s) along the steam table and the 2 door prep top cooler are heavily scratched and scored. The food contact surface is no longer easily cleaned and sanitized due to condition. Also the cutting boards used for cutting vegetables and meats are also heavily scratched and scored.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces such as cutting blocks and boards that are subject to scratching and scoring shall be resurfaced if they can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized, or discarded if they are not capable of being resurfaced. PIC TOLD EHS THAT NEW CUTTING BOARDS HAS ALREADY BEEN PURCHASED FOR CUTTING VEGETABLES AND MEATS BUT WILL LOOK INTO REPLACING THE STEAM WELL AND 2DR PREP TOP UNIT CUTTING BOARDS BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): in the walk-in refrigerator, a milk crate was being used to store bottled waters off of the floor. A milk crate was also used to store dry and clean sanitizer towels under a prep sink in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. PLEASE MAKE SURE TO GET RID OF ALL MILK CRATES BY THE TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION. BRIGHTVIEW DULLES CORNER (Inspection Date: 06/17/2026) Page 3 of 4

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Hard Wood
violations.observation: Unsealed wood or wood wicker is used in contact with food. An unsealed cutting board used to serve charcuterie.
violations.corrective_action: Wood and wood wicker may not be used as a food-contact surface unless the wood is hard maple or close-grained and used for cutting boards, cutting blocks, bakers' tables, and utensils such as rolling pins, doughnut dowels, salad bowls, and chopsticks. PLEASE MAKE SURE TO GET RID OF ALL UNSEALED WOOD BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: underneath multiple prep tables around the kitchen had a build up of debris and dirt.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT UNDERNEATH ALL PREP TABLES NEEDS TO BE CLEANED BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: EHS smelled a strong odor coming from multiple drains in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. PLEASE CALL A TECHNICIAN TO LOOK AT PLUMBING SYSTEM. EHS WILL CONDUCT A FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION TO MAKE SURE ODOR IS GONE. EHS WILL REACH OUT TO PIC TO SCHEDULE FOLLOW-UP.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed the wall behind the stand mixer in the kitchen was dirty to sight and touch, the wall behind the cook line is also in need of a deep cleaning and is dirty to sight and touch.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. PLEASE CLEAN ALL WALLS BEHIND PREP EQUIPMENT BY TIME OF FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. OBSERVED EMPLOYEE HANDLE RAW SALMON WITH GLOVED HANDS, CHANGE TASKS/GLOVES, BUT DID NOT WASH HANDS.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EMPLOYEE WASHED HANDS AND PUT ON NEW GLOVES.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Water Temp
violations.observation: The handwashing sink NEAR THE DISHWASHING MACHINE REACHED MAXIMUM TEMPERATURE OF 75F DURING INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: A handwashing sink shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 100F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. PIC INFORMED MAINTENANCE TEAM OF ISSUE DURING INSPECTION AND WILL SEND EHS PROOF OF CORRECTION WITHIN 10 DAYS.

out_items.name: Hot and cold water available, adequate pressure

violations.title: Water Pressure Meets Facility Demands
violations.observation: Hot water under inadequate pressure was found to serve the following equipment: HANDWASHING SINK NEAR DISHWASHING MACHINE.
violations.corrective_action: Water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water. PIC CONTACTED MAINTENANCE TEAM DURING INSPECTION AND WILL ENSURE PROOF OF CORRECTION IS SENT TO EHS WITHIN 10 DAYS.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: The sink basin AT THE HANDWASHING SINK NEAR THE KITCHEN OFFICE AND ACROSS FROM GRILL-LINE is slow to drain.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. PIC CONTACTED MAINTENANCE TEAM DURING INSPECTION AND WILL PROVIDE PROOF OF CORRECTION TO EHS WITHIN 10 DAYS.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Water Temp
violations.observation: OBSERVED NO HANDWASHING SINKS MEET 100F DURING INSPECTION; TEMPERATURE RANGED FROM 64-98F FOR ALL HANDWASHING SINKS.
violations.corrective_action: A handwashing sink shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 100F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. PIC WILL CONTACT BUILDING ENGINEER TO FIX HANDWASHING SINK TEMPERATURES AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. PLEASE ENSURE CORRECTION BY DECEMBER 19TH.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED BAKED BEANS IN TWO-DOOR STACKED CABINET HOT HOLDING UNIT AT 109-117F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. PIC REHEATED BEANS TO 165F DUING INSPECTION AND UNDERSTANDS HOT HOLDING FOODS MUST BE KEPT AT 135F OR ABOVE.
